_comment: UI texts of Paradox Modding Tool. German (de.json) is the source language. How to translate: see TRANSLATING.md.
menu.games.heading: Open game in a new window:
menu.mods.tip: Choose the active mod (fixed or automatic from the open file) and manage the mods of this game
menu.myMods.tip: Overview of your own mods for all games: Steam numbers, bugs, releases and alerts
menu.tile.gui.tip: GUI inspector, data helper, building blocks, new GUI file and the mod's GUI settings
menu.project.tip: Copy, move or compare the active file between the mods of a project
menu.project.copy: Copy active file to another mod
menu.project.move: Move active file to another mod
menu.project.compare: Compare active file with another mod
menu.project.sync.tip: Compare two mods of the project folder by folder and take over single files
menu.cuTool.tip: Compare and Update Tool: compare two files or folders (Compare) and check mod files against vanilla, with a 3-way merge after game updates (Update). U takes marked lines into the other side. Replace lists replace saved words in a mod folder with one button, e.g. after a game patch.
menu.patchRecipes.tip: Patch recipes: repeatable rule patches for the mod (table plus rules), applied again after every vanilla update
patchUi.title: Patch recipes
patchUi.noGameFolder: Game folder not found: please choose the game (its executable) in the settings
patchUi.deleteConfirm: Delete recipe "{0}"? The recipe's memory is deleted too; generated regions in the mod files stay.
patchUi.noRecipe: No recipe yet. Create one with "New recipe".
patchUi.recipesMoved: Moved {0} recipe files from the mod folder to {1} so they are not uploaded.
patchUi.recipesKept: Not moved because they already exist at the new location: {0}. They remain in {1}; please check them by hand and remove them before uploading.
patchUi.recipesMoveFailed: Recipes could not be moved out of the mod folder: {0}
patchUi.stale: Files have changed since the preview. Please compute the preview again.
patchUi.unsaved: {0} is open in the editor and not saved.
patchUi.writeFailed: Writing failed, all files were reset: {0}
patchUi.columns.title: Columns
patchUi.columns.name: Name
patchUi.plan.title: Computing preview
patchUi.plan.hint: The rules run on a copy in memory; nothing is written.
patchUi.result.title: Result of "{0}" for {1}
patchUi.field.name: Name
patchUi.edit.enabled.tip: When switched off, the edit stays in the recipe but does not run.
patchUi.field.createCopy: Create a copy from vanilla if it is missing
patchUi.preview.noPlan: No preview yet. "Compute preview" runs the rules without writing anything.
patchUi.preview.dropped: Recipe changed, compute the preview again
patchUi.preview.conflicts: Units with conflicts: your version on the left, newly generated on the right. Take what should stay with U.
patchUi.preview.conflictsConfirm: {0} files with conflicts will not be written. Apply anyway?
patchUi.reapplyAfterUpdate: This mod has patch recipes. Open them now to apply them again after the update?
patchUi.preview.noRows: The table has no rows, so there is nothing to do. Read rows in or add some first (Table tab).
patchUi.rules.wholeRows: Rows completely or not at all
patchUi.rules.wholeRows.tip: If one rule skips a row (e.g. “already defined”), all rules leave it out. This way no row is left half converted.
patchUi.columns.match.tip: Separate several searches with ;, e.g. special_building_slot = {key}; special_building = {key}
patchUi.columns.all.tip: All hits as a list (a, b, c) instead of the first. In templates, {*column}…{/column} repeats a text for each value.
patchUi.field.vanillaPathsOnly: Only files that also exist in vanilla
patchUi.field.vanillaPathsOnly.tip: Acts only on mod copies of vanilla files. The mod's own files in the same folder stay untouched.
patchUi.field.adoptExisting.tip: If a key is already defined elsewhere in the mod, PMT moves that block into the generated region, converts it with the edits and removes it from its file. Your changes in it are kept.
patchUi.preview.adoptionLost: Not applied: {0} would be lost. The adopted unit was taken back with U, but its removal from the source file was not. Take back both or neither, or compute the preview again.
patchUi.new.preset: From preset: special buildings into normal buildings
patchUi.import.button.tip: Lists the special buildings from vanilla. Chosen ones become table rows, existing rows stay.
patchUi.import.noPlace.tip: No place in history: vanilla grants the slot by script (event, decision or great project) and builds the building right away, e.g. generic mines, Pleasure Dome, Forbidden City. Converted it would be buildable everywhere and the scripts would fail; so it stays special and cannot be selected.
patchUi.adoptMod.button.tip: Renames buildings your mod keeps under its own name as a copy of a vanilla building back to the vanilla key. Afterwards the specials become rows of the table.
patchUi.adoptMod.none: No buildings with their own name found that only your mod defines
patchUi.adoptMod.noProposals: No proposals: all {0} buildings are your own, without a vanilla counterpart
patchUi.adoptMod.status.targetInVanilla: vanilla defines it in {0}, the mod does not override the file
patchUi.adoptMod.saveWarning: Renaming {0} buildings breaks running save games of this mod: buildings already built disappear. Continue?
patchUi.adoptMod.planReady: Rename of {0} buildings ready. Apply writes it as one undo step; afterwards the specials become rows of the table
patchUi.adoptMod.done: {0} buildings renamed, {1} taken as rows. The preview now shows the recipe run
patchUi.watch.patterns.tip: Patterns the watcher searches for; it always also searches the keys of the table rows
patchUi.watch.patterns.prompt: One pattern per line, e.g. every_special_building_province. Only whole words count, spaces do not matter.
patchUi.watch.copyAndRule.tip: Adds the file to a line rule and turns on “Create a copy from vanilla” there; the copy is created on the next apply
patchUi.watch.notScanned: Not scanned yet. “Scan again” searches vanilla and the mod.
patchUi.watch.filesChanged: Files changed since the scan (Apply), scan again
patchUi.watch.ruleAddedDisabled: File added to the rule “{0}”. The rule is switched off: switch it on in the Rules tab, or the file stays not covered.
patchUi.watch.cancelled: Scan cancelled, the previous result stays
patchUi.watch.scanHint: Vanilla and the mod are searched for the search patterns and row keys. Nothing is written.
patchUi.watch.ruleAdded: File added to the rule “{0}”. The copy is created on the next apply.
patchUi.watch.ruleSibling: New rule “{0}” created for this file only. It copies the file from vanilla on the next apply.
patchUi.watch.ruleCreated: New line rule created, it is still switched off
patchUi.field.files.tip: Path from the game folder; * and ** for folders, separate several patterns with ;
settings.hotkey.patch.take: Take marked lines back in the preview
menu.modCompat.tip: Check mods against each other: file and key conflicts, whether overrides make sense, and a report for compatibility patches
menu.compatch.tip: Merge two mods and write the result as a compatibility patch or into an own mod
menu.scriptDocs.tip: Look up modifiers, triggers, effects, event targets and more (from the game's documentation logs)
menu.templates.tip: Create several blocks (and matching localisation) with counted-up numbers from a sample snippet
menu.help.checkUpdates.tip: Look for a newer version on GitHub
menu.help.reportBug: Report a bug in the tool
menu.help.reportBug.tip: Opens a new GitHub issue with program version and system details
menu.help.changelog.tip: Opens the list of changes per version (Readme\Changelog.txt)
menu.help.changelog.missing: Readme\Changelog.txt is missing in the program folder.
menu.help.noRepository: Not available yet: no GitHub repository is set in AppInfo.GitHubRepository.
menu.toolbar.undo.tip: Undo the last program action, for example saving or replacing in files
menu.toolbar.redo.tip: Redo the last undone program action
menu.toolbar.search.tip: Search & replace, also in all files of a folder (Ctrl+F)
menu.toolbar.goToLine.tip: Jump to a line in the active document (Ctrl+G)
menu.toolbar.goToBracket.tip: Jump to the bracket that matches the one at the cursor (Ctrl+B); a second jump goes back
menu.toolbar.scopeFinder.tip: Build scope chains or find paths between scopes, e.g. from root to owner.capital (Ctrl+Shift+P)
menu.toolbar.format.tip: Remove surplus spaces and blank lines or reformat the structure of the active document; undo with Ctrl+Z
menu.toolbar.notes.tip: Personal note on the active file. It is kept in the program, not in the file.
menu.toolbar.bookmark.tip: Set, change or remove a bookmark with a comment at the selection or cursor line; Ctrl+F2 quickly sets one without a comment
menu.toolbar.bug.tip: Create a new bug for the active file or attach this spot to an existing report, with the caret line or selection as the line link
menu.toolbar.splitView.tip: Split the screen into two workspaces
menu.toolbar.explorer.tip: Show or hide the directory overview
menu.toolbar.notesPanel.tip: Show or hide the right panel with the note and bookmarks of the active file
menu.toolbar.autoComplete.tip: Turn the suggestion list while typing (auto-completion of script names) on or off
menu.toolbar.hover.tip: Turn the tooltip with description and scopes when hovering modifiers, triggers and effects on or off
menu.toolbar.launchOption.tip: Launch option for the game (from the active game profile)
menu.toolbar.playset.tip: Playset to launch with (from playsets.json); set as the active playset on launch if different
menu.toolbar.launchGame.tip: Starts the configured game .exe with the chosen launch option
menu.workspace.new.tip: New empty document in this workspace
menu.workspace.open.tip: Open a file in this workspace
menu.workspace.save.tip: Save the active document of this workspace (Ctrl+S)
menu.workspace.saveAll.tip: Save all unsaved documents of both workspaces (Ctrl+Shift+S)
menu.workspace.close.tip: Close the active document of this workspace
menu.workspace.move.tip: Move the active document to the other workspace
menu.workspace.category.tip: Set the category of the active document (overrides the automatic assignment)
menu.workspace.filter.tip: Choose which filter check boxes the document bar shows
menu.workspace.icons.tip: Choose which icons are shown next to the documents
menu.workspace.sort.tip: Order of this workspace's tabs: manual (drag) or automatic by name, category or origin
menu.workspace.sort.name: Name

errorlog.export.tip: Save the filtered list as a text or CSV file

settings.menu.tip: Opens the settings window. Changes take effect immediately.
settings.window.title: Settings
settings.general.gamePath.tip: Selects the game's .exe (for example EU 5.exe in the binaries folder). ▶ Launch game uses this path.
settings.general.playsets.tip: Selects playsets.json (under Documents/Paradox Interactive/<game>). Needed to pick a playset when launching.
settings.general.storage.tip: Choose the parent folder for "[mod name] Snapshots" and the vanilla history, or (not recommended) store them in the mod folder
settings.general.relearnLoc.tip: Reads the game's script and loc files again and learns which places (object names with suffixes, fields such as text) need a localization (otherwise happens automatically after game updates)
settings.general.relearnScope.tip: Reads the vanilla files again and learns the start scopes of fields and the names of script values from them (otherwise happens automatically after game updates and new documentation logs)
settings.reorder.hint: Drag a row or move it with the arrows; Alt+↑/↓ on the keyboard
settings.workspace.splitView.tip: Splits the screen into two workspaces (same switch as in the toolbar)
settings.workspace.explorer.tip: Shows or hides the folder overview (same switch as in the toolbar). It is always visible when the program starts.
settings.workspace.bracket.tip: Colors the bracket at the cursor and its counterpart ({ }, ( ), [ ]). Ctrl+B still jumps to the matching bracket when highlighting is off.
settings.workspace.autoComplete.tip: Suggestion list while typing (from 3 characters) and with Ctrl+Space, from the script database. When off, Ctrl+Space shows no suggestions either.
settings.workspace.completeCustomLoc.tip: Adds the game's custom localizations (e.g. GetName) to the suggestion list (default: off). The hover tooltip knows them regardless.
settings.workspace.documentBar.tip: Shows or hides the category checkboxes and filters (with notes/bookmarks) above the tabs
settings.workspace.multiRowTabs.tip: Shows the open documents in several rows instead of one scrolling row (default: off)
settings.workspace.pathBar.tip: Row above the editor with the path, copy, open folder and show notes (default: on)
settings.workspace.replaceWarningsWindow: Show warnings after replacing in their own window

Reports OR, NOR and AND blocks that have only one entry or none after replacing in a separate window instead of the notes panel (default: off). If the notes panel is switched off, the window is always used.
settings.workspace.scopeStatusBar: Show scope in the status bar
settings.workspace.scopeStatusBar.tip: Shows the scope at the cursor below the editor, with the path to it (field, iterators, event targets)
settings.workspace.scopeStatusBarTop: Show scope below the path bar
settings.workspace.scopeStatusBarTop.tip: Also shows the same scope line right below the path bar above the editor (default: off). Independent of the bar below the editor.
settings.workspace.scopeWarnings: Scope warnings in the text (wavy line)
settings.workspace.scopeWarnings.tip: Underlines triggers and effects that are not valid in the current scope. Reported only where the scope is certain.
settings.workspace.scriptHover.tip: Shows a tooltip with description and scopes when the mouse rests on a known modifier/trigger/effect (from the script database)
settings.workspace.scopeHover: Show scope in the hover tooltip
settings.workspace.scopeHover.tip: Adds to the hover tooltip whether the trigger/effect is allowed in the current scope
settings.workspace.modifierHover: Show modifier values as in game
settings.workspace.modifierHover.tip: When hovering a modifier number or script value, shows the value the game displays.
settings.workspace.modifierNames.tip: Adds the translated modifier name (from the game's localization) after the value in the modifier tooltip.
menu.toolbar.modifierReload.tip: Rereads formats, script values, constants and modifier names from the game and the mod, e.g. after changing script_values files
editor.modifierReloaded: Modifier values reloaded: {0} formats, {1} script values, {2} names
settings.workspace.resultsOnTop.tip: Sets whether the search results bar appears above or below the workspace (default: below)
settings.wsToolbar.categories.tip: Create, rename and color file categories and give them extension and folder rules
settings.wsToolbar.filterHint: Same entries as the "Filter" menu. A hidden checkbox no longer filters; its files are always visible.
settings.wsToolbar.iconHint: Same entries as the "Icons" menu. Only changes the display; filters such as "Only with note" keep working.
settings.wsToolbar.filterButton: Show the filter button in the toolbar
settings.wsToolbar.filterButton.tip: The "Filter ▾" button in the toolbar of each workspace
settings.wsToolbar.iconButton: Show the icon button in the toolbar
settings.wsToolbar.iconButton.tip: The "Icons ▾" button in the toolbar of each workspace
settings.errorLog.standalone: Error log as a separate window
settings.errorLog.standalone.tip: The window does not stay above PMT and has its own taskbar entry, e.g. for a second screen. Applies the next time the window opens.
settings.errorLog.placement: PMT remembers the window's position and size. As a separate window it opens on a different screen than PMT the first time, if one is connected.
settings.saveExplorer.standalone: Save explorer as a separate window
settings.saveExplorer.standalone.tip: The window does not stay on top of PMT and has its own taskbar entry, for example for a second screen. Applies the next time the window opens.
settings.saveExplorer.placement: PMT remembers the window's position and size. As a separate window it opens on a different screen than PMT the first time, if one is connected.
settings.listSearch.tip: Search the list: Enter picks the first match, Down arrow moves into the list, Escape clears the search (a second Escape closes the list).
settings.notes.visible.tip: Right panel with the note and bookmarks of the active file (default: on)
settings.notes.keepOpen: Keep panel open for files without notes
settings.notes.keepOpen.tip: Without this setting the panel hides for files without note and bookmarks. With it the panel stays open, so the view does not jump when you switch files.
settings.notes.scope: Show scope in the notes panel

rulehelp.title: Guide: Counting rules
rulehelp.whatIs.heading: What is a rule?
rulehelp.whatIs.intro: For every number in your snippet, the template generator decides whether it is counted up. A counting rule tells it exactly what to do for certain names, for example: “In names like iv2_ga_select_historic_ARA_1_1, only the number after ARA counts”. You create the rule once, and from then on it applies every time you generate.
rulehelp.whatIs.parts:
A rule consists of three parts:
1. Pattern: Which names are meant?
2. Where: Anywhere in the snippet or only inside a certain entry?
3. Action: What happens to the numbers of these names?
rulehelp.whatIs.quickest: The quickest way: right-click a number in the snippet and choose “Create rule from this number” (or pick a row in the counting points list and click “Create rule”). The dialog is then already filled in; you only need to make the pattern more general with * if the rule should apply to more names.
rulehelp.parts.heading: The parts of a rule
rulehelp.parts.name: Name: Just for you, so you can find the rule in the list again. It also appears as the reason when you click a number (“Rule “…” (layer)”).
rulehelp.parts.layer:
Layer: Where the rule is saved and whom it applies to.
• Template: only for the template that is currently open.
• Mod: for all templates of this mod (you choose the mod in the “Mod:” field of the template window).
• Game: for all mods of this game.
• All games: for several games; there you choose which ones.
rulehelp.parts.where:
Where:
• Anywhere: every name in the snippet.
• Inside key: only in the entry “key = …”, that is in the value and, for blocks, in everything inside it. Example: the key position applies to “position = { 105 37 }”.
rulehelp.parts.action:
Action:
• Ignore: No number of the name counts.
• Only marked counts: Only the number at [#] counts, the other numbers of the name do not.
• All count: All numbers of the name count, including name numbers as in ck3_… and single numbers like “cost = 10”.
• Marked does not count: Only the number at [#] does not count. The other rules still decide about the other numbers of the name.
rulehelp.patterns.heading: The pattern language
rulehelp.patterns.syntax:
*     any text (including nothing)
#     a number (a whole run of digits)
[#]   the number in question (at most once per pattern)
Text  exactly this text; case does not matter
rulehelp.patterns.important:
Important:
• The pattern must match the whole name, not just part of it. “button” only matches the name “button”; “*button*” matches every name that contains button.
• Quotation marks are not part of the pattern. For a string like "Idea 5" you write Idea [#].
• # always stands for a whole number. “iv#*” matches iv2_ga_… and iv23_x (with the number 23).
• If you write several patterns one below the other (one per line), it is enough if one of them matches.
• You can turn on “Match case” in the dialog.
rulehelp.examples.heading: Examples to try
rulehelp.examples.one: Example 1: Only the number after ARA should count.
rulehelp.examples.oneBox:
Name in snippet:  iv2_ga_select_historic_ARA_1_1
Pattern:          iv#_ga_*_ARA_[#]_#
Where:            Anywhere
Action:           Only marked counts

Result: Three passes produce
  iv2_ga_select_historic_ARA_1_1
  iv2_ga_select_historic_ARA_2_1
  iv2_ga_select_historic_ARA_3_1
rulehelp.examples.oneNote: If the last number (the level) should count instead, move the marker there: iv#_ga_*_ARA_#_[#]
rulehelp.examples.twoBox:
String in snippet:  "Idea 5 of 10"
Pattern:            Idea # of [#]
Action:             Only marked counts

Result: The 10 counts, so “Idea 5 of 10” becomes “Idea 5 of 11”.
rulehelp.examples.three: Example 3: Ignore all names containing “button” (this is how the built-in rule “Button” is built).
rulehelp.examples.four: Example 4: Ignore everything in position (this is how the built-in rule “position entry” is built).
rulehelp.examples.fourBox:
Pattern:    *
Where:      Inside key
Key:        position
Action:     Ignore
rulehelp.examples.five: Example 5: The number directly after a prefix should never count, but the other numbers should count as usual (this is how the built-in rule “Name prefix” is built).
rulehelp.examples.fiveBox:
Patterns (two lines):  iv[#]*
                       iv_[#]*
Action:                Marked does not count

Result: In iv_2_tooltip_idea_1_1 the 2 does not count; the 1 after idea still counts
according to the “Multiple numbers” setting (first counts).
rulehelp.examples.six: Example 6: The same rule for a whole mod or only for one template. Create the rule on the “Mod” layer if it should apply to all templates of this mod, and on the “Template” layer if only this template needs it. Later you can bring a rule to another layer with “Move”, or also add it on a second layer with “Create copy”.
rulehelp.order.heading: Precedence and layers
rulehelp.order.text:
• The “Counting rules” window lists the rules in the order in which they are checked: first the template, then Mod, Game, All games and finally the built-in ones. Within a layer, the order of the list decides; you change it with “Move up” and “Move down”.
• For each number, the first rule that has a result for it decides. If a rule matches the name but not this number (for example “Marked does not count” for a different number), the next rule decides.
• The check marks in the counting points list and the boxes for each name shape take precedence over every rule. Examples in the snippet that really change (idea_1, idea_2, idea_3 …) take precedence over rules that turn counting off.
• The check mark in front of a rule turns it on or off. For a rule from a less specific layer (including the built-in ones), the check mark only affects the layer chosen at the top: turned off on “Template”, this applies to this template; on “Mod”, to all templates of the mod.
• Built-in rules cannot be changed. Use “Create copy” to make your own version; the original is turned off on the chosen layer.
rulehelp.troubleshoot.heading: My rule has no effect
rulehelp.troubleshoot.text:
Go through this list:
• The “Hits” column shows 0: the pattern does not match the whole name. Check the start and the end (is a * missing?) and look at the preview in the dialog, where you see the matches right away.
• Case: if “Match case” is turned on in the dialog, the case must be right.
• The actions “Only marked counts” and “Marked does not count” need a [#] in every pattern.
• Is the rule turned on (check mark) and is it on a layer that applies? The “Mod” layer only exists when a mod is chosen in the template window. Rules on “All games” only apply to the games entered there.
• A rule further up in the list may decide about the same number first.
• A check mark or box in the counting points list takes precedence over the rule.
• If the snippet contains several examples with counted-up numbers, the generator learns the counting from them and ignores rules that turn counting off there.
• Click the number in the snippet: the status bar shows which rule decides about it.
patchhelp.title: Guide: Patch recipes
patchhelp.intro.heading: What are patch recipes for?
patchhelp.intro.what: Some changes to a mod follow the same pattern in many files. Example: every special building is to become a normal building. To do this, you comment out the slot line in the history, copy the building block from vanilla, remove type = special, add the building to the holdings and so on, for every building separately.
patchhelp.intro.how: A patch recipe describes this work once: as a table (what) and rules (how). PMT then does it for all rows of the table. After a vanilla update, you simply apply the recipe again.
patchhelp.intro.where: Recipes belong to one mod but are stored outside its folder: in PMT's storage location (default: Documents\Paradox Modding Tool) in the folder "<mod name> Patch Recipes", next to the snapshots. This way they are never uploaded. PMT automatically moves recipes from the former .pmt-patches folder inside the mod there when you open them.
patchhelp.steps.heading: The workflow in four steps
patchhelp.steps.list:
1. Recipe: choose the mod, then “New recipe”.
2. Table: one row per thing you want to change (for example per building), with columns for everything that differs per row.
3. Rules: what should happen to each row.
4. Preview: run the rules as a trial, check the result, then “Apply”.
patchhelp.steps.safety: PMT writes nothing until you apply. Before applying, PMT makes a backup of the mod. In the main window, “Undo” reverts the whole run in one step.
patchhelp.table.heading: The table
patchhelp.table.key: Every row has a key (column key), for example angkor_wat_01. It must be unique.
patchhelp.table.own: You add your own columns under “Columns”: name, type (Text, Number or List) and default. An empty cell uses the default, which is shown in grey in the cell. Separate the values of a list with commas.
patchhelp.table.derived: You do not type derived columns. PMT looks them up in the game files. They are grey and cannot be edited.
patchhelp.table.derivedBox:
Column province_id (derived)
  Files:   history/provinces/*.txt
  Source:  Vanilla
  Search:  special_building_slot = {key}
  Take:    outermost block

Column barony (derived, Check title)
  Files:   common/landed_titles/**/*.txt
  Source:  Vanilla
  Search:  province = {province_id}
  Take:    innermost block

Result for angkor_wat_01:
  province_id = 10816      (the block that contains the slot)
  barony      = b_angkor   (the block that contains province = 10816)
patchhelp.table.order: A derived column may use earlier columns, as barony uses {province_id} here. That is why the order of the columns matters.
patchhelp.table.source: Source: “Vanilla” searches the game files, “Mod” only your mod, “Mod before vanilla” the mod first. “Optional” means: not found gives an empty value instead of an error.
patchhelp.table.errors:
Rows marked red have an error; the reason is in the “Note” column:
• The key is missing or appears twice.
• A derived value was not found (except with “Optional”).
• A title in a column with “Check title” does not exist, for example b_bamiyan.
patchhelp.table.skip: PMT skips red rows in all rules with scope “per row”. What these rows generated earlier stays in place. All other rows run normally. “Only entries with errors” shows only the red rows.
patchhelp.placeholders.heading: Placeholders
patchhelp.placeholders.intro: In searches, paths and texts, PMT inserts the values for each row:
patchhelp.placeholders.box:
{key}                    key of the row
{column}                 value of the column, for example {barony}
{?column}Text{/column}   text only if the column has a value
{!column}Text{/column}   text only if the column is empty
patchhelp.placeholders.list: A list column in a path or list entry creates one target per value. With holdings = castle_holding, city_holding, {holdings}/buildings affects both holdings.
patchhelp.placeholders.empty: An unknown placeholder is an error in the rule editor. If a value is empty, the rule skips this row. The preview gives the reason (“empty value for …”).
patchhelp.rules.heading: The rule kinds
patchhelp.rules.order: The rules run from top to bottom. Scope “per row” runs for every table row, “once (global)” once for the whole recipe. The “Active” check box turns a rule off without deleting it.
patchhelp.rules.lines: Lines: finds lines in files of your mod and changes them.
patchhelp.rules.linesBox:
Files:   history/provinces/*.txt
Search:  special_building_slot = {key}
Action:  Comment out

Before:  special_building_slot = angkor_wat_01
After:   #special_building_slot = angkor_wat_01
patchhelp.rules.linesActions: Actions: Comment out, Delete, Replace (only the found text) and Remove block (the whole block with this key; with “Include upgrade levels” also all levels via next_building). With “Create a copy from vanilla if it is missing”, PMT first creates the mod file from vanilla. Search type “Text” matches whole words only and ignores differences in spaces: province does not match every_province.
patchhelp.rules.blockCopy: Block copy: copies a block from vanilla into your mod and changes it on the way.
patchhelp.rules.template: Template: writes a separate text for each row into a file, optionally into a specific block (“Inside”).
patchhelp.rules.list: List: adds an entry to a list if it is missing there.
patchhelp.rules.showResult: “Show result” shows what the selected rule changes for the row under “Preview for”: current on the left, after applying on the right. This lets you check a rule without computing the whole preview.
patchhelp.preview.heading: Preview and apply
patchhelp.preview.compute: “Compute preview” runs all active rules on a copy in memory. Every file gets a status: new, changed, conflict or unchanged.
patchhelp.preview.files: Clicking a file shows the current text on the left and the result on the right. If you mark lines on the right and press U, PMT takes this change back. Skipped rows and warnings are listed below the list.
patchhelp.preview.apply: “Apply” writes all files at once. PMT refuses if files have changed since the preview or are open unsaved in the editor. Then save and compute the preview again.
patchhelp.memory.heading: Generated regions and your manual edits
patchhelp.memory.markers: Block copy and template write between markers:
patchhelp.memory.edit: You may edit the text between the markers by hand, but not the marker lines themselves. If you delete a PMT-Unit line together with its block, the unit counts as deleted by hand and PMT does not generate it again.
patchhelp.memory.merge:
PMT remembers what it wrote last. On the next run:
• If you have not changed the unit, PMT replaces it with the new version.
• If you have changed it, PMT merges your change with the new version.
• If both change the same place, the preview shows a conflict: your version on the left, newly generated on the right. Take what should stay with U, then “Accept as resolved”.
patchhelp.memory.lists: In lists, PMT removes only entries that it added itself. It never touches entries that were there before.
patchhelp.memory.limit: Limit: line rules have no memory. What you take back with U in the preview comes back on the next run. Turn the rule off or change its search instead.
patchhelp.update.heading: After a vanilla update
patchhelp.update.steps:
1. In the Compare and Update Tool, run “Merge after game update”.
2. If the mod has recipes, PMT then asks whether to open them.
3. Compute the preview, check it, apply.
patchhelp.update.result: This way new vanilla content, for example changed building costs, ends up in your generated blocks. Your manual edits are kept.
patchhelp.trouble.heading: My recipe does not work
patchhelp.trouble.list:
• A file is missing from the preview: check the file pattern. Paths start in the game folder (common/…), ** includes subfolders.
• A row is red: the reason is in the “Note” column.
• “already defined in …”: the key already exists elsewhere in the mod. PMT does not create it twice. Use “Adopt existing blocks” (button in the preview): PMT moves your block into the generated region, converts it and keeps your changes.
• A rule changes nothing: is “Active” checked? Search type “Text” matches whole words only.
• “empty value for …”: the row has no value and no default in a column that is used.
• When in doubt: “Show result” for a single row.
patchhelp.rules.wholeRows: “Rows completely or not at all” (below the rule list): if one rule skips a row, all rules leave it out. The preview gives the reason (“left out as in rule …”).
patchhelp.preset.defaults: The preset turns on “Adopt existing blocks” and “Rows completely or not at all” from the start. This way no building is left half converted: if a building cannot be converted, its slots and holdings stay unchanged too.
patchhelp.rules.linesMulti: The action Replace with the search kind "Text" also finds matches across several lines. A block in multi-line form (building_requirement_castle_city_church =, line break, { LEVEL = 03 } below) is replaced like the one-line form; comments stay untouched.
patchhelp.rules.blockCopyInsert: "Insert into" only adds text and replaces nothing: if the block (e.g. on_start) does not exist, PMT creates it, otherwise the text goes to its end. For adopted blocks PMT inserts only the lines that are still missing. "Insert after", "Insert at start" and "Insert at end" pick another place.
patchhelp.preset.resource:
In addition to the five rules the preset creates four rules trigger_level_01 to trigger_level_04 and extends the block copy. Both belong to the mod "Flogi's Buildings and Technology Mod":
• The block copy inserts into every converted building (every upgrade level) the effects flogis_techmod_subtract_wood/stone/metal/luxury_250 in on_start and flogis_techmod_add_wood/stone/metal/luxury_250 in on_cancelled. If on_start or on_cancelled already exists, the lines go into it; for adopted blocks only the missing ones.
• The four rules replace building_requirement_castle_city_church = { LEVEL = 01 } to 04 in the generated buildings with building_requirement_main_building = { LEVEL = 2 }, 4, 6 and 8, in one-line and multi-line form.
If you do not need this, switch off the four rules and, in the block copy, the two edits "Insert into" with on_start and on_cancelled.
patchUi.watch.ignoreFolder.tip: Ignores all files in the folder of the selected file, including subfolders.
patchUi.watch.unignore.tip: Stops ignoring. If the file was ignored through a folder, the folder rule is removed and all files of the folder count again.
patchUi.rules.topUp: Add what is missing from the preset
patchUi.rules.topUp.tip: Adds what the recipe lacks compared with its preset: rules, columns, edits and watcher search patterns. Existing items stay unchanged.
patchUi.rules.topUp.none: The recipe lacks nothing from the preset.
patchhelp.watch.folder: "Ignore folder" ignores all files in the folder of the selected file, including subfolders (e.g. common/customizable_localization), in one step. "Stop ignoring" on one of these files removes the folder rule; then all files of the folder count again.
patchhelp.preset.topUp: A recipe created from a preset does not get new rules of the preset by itself. "Add what is missing from the preset" (Rules tab, below the rule list) shows what the recipe lacks: rules, columns, edits in existing rules and watcher search patterns. After a confirmation PMT adds only that. Existing rules, hand changes and switched-off rules stay unchanged; an edit you deleted comes back.
patchUi.blockEdit.copy.tip: If the block exists only in vanilla, PMT first creates the mod copy of that vanilla file and edits the block there. If it is already in a mod file, it is edited there.
patchUi.new.presetResources: From preset: resources in special buildings
patchhelp.rules.blockEdit: Edit block: changes a block directly in the existing files of your mod, without a copy and without its own target file. The edits are the same as in the block copy. If the block exists only in vanilla, PMT first creates the mod file with "Create copy from vanilla if missing". With "Include follow-up levels" the rule applies to all levels via next_building. PMT only inserts lines that are still missing; a second run changes nothing.
patchhelp.preset2.heading: Preset: resources in special buildings
patchhelp.preset2.text: Inserts resource effects into special buildings without converting them; whether a building has a place in the history does not matter. Meant for specials that stay special because a script assigns their slot (e.g. generic mines, pleasure palace). The preset has only one rule "Edit block": it inserts the effects flogis_techmod_subtract_wood/stone/metal/luxury_250 into on_start and flogis_techmod_add_wood/stone/metal/luxury_250 into on_cancelled, in all levels of the chain and directly in the existing files. "Read specials from vanilla" lists all specials that start a chain. Specials that the preset "Special buildings into normal buildings" converts get the effects there already; do not add them here as well. The effects belong to the mod "Flogi's Buildings and Technology Mod"; change them in the rule if you do not need them.
patchhelp.table.all: You separate several searches with ; (each one counts). With “All hits (list)” a derived column returns all findings as a list instead of only the first. Later columns that use it then search once per value.
patchhelp.placeholders.repeat: {*column}Text{/column} repeats the text once per list value; inside it, {column} stands for the single value. The preset uses this for OR = { barony = title:… }.
patchhelp.rules.options: Two options: “Only files that also exist in vanilla” (Lines) acts only on mod copies of vanilla files and protects the mod's own files in the same folder. “Adopt existing blocks” (Block copy) is explained in the preset section.
patchhelp.preset.heading: Preset: special buildings into normal buildings
patchhelp.preset.intro: For CK III, “New recipe” offers the preset “special buildings into normal buildings”. It creates the columns holdings, provinz and barony, five rules in a fixed order and the watcher's search patterns. provinz and barony search all four forms in history and all places.
patchhelp.preset.rulesBox:
slots       Comment out slot lines in history (all four forms)
iterators   Replace every_/any_/random_/ordered_special_building_province,
            you add files through the watcher
originals   Remove the original definitions from the mod copies of vanilla files
buildings   Copy buildings from vanilla, remove type = special,
            insert OR = { barony = title:… } into can_construct_potential
holdings    Add the buildings to the holdings
patchhelp.preset.import: “Read specials from vanilla” in the table lists every vanilla special that starts an upgrade chain. You see the baronies found, whether your mod still defines the building as a special and whether it is already a row. Nothing is pre-checked. “Only still special in mod” shows the buildings you can still convert.
patchhelp.preset.adopt: If a building already exists in your mod, the preview reports “already defined” and offers “Adopt existing blocks”. PMT then moves your block into the generated region, converts it (type = special out, barony in) and removes it from its file. Your other changes stay as hand edits, and future vanilla changes are merged in.
patchhelp.preset.limits:
Limits:
• Specials without a place in history (e.g. generic mines, Pleasure Dome, Forbidden City) stay special: their slot comes from a script (event, decision, great project) that builds the building right away. The import dialog shows “no place” and does not let you select them; such a row in the recipe is red (“provinz: not found”) and every rule leaves it out.
• Lines of later upgrade levels in history (e.g. special_building = holy_site_canterbury_cathedral_02) are not covered by the rule slots; the watcher shows them.
• Buildings that history places at game start are missing at game start after the conversion.
patchhelp.adoptMod.heading: Adopting existing mod buildings
patchhelp.adoptMod.intro: If your mod once copied vanilla buildings under its own names (e.g. flogis_techmod_special_building_1_0 for holy_site_cathedral_01), "Bestehende Mod-Gebäude übernehmen" in the table renames them back to the vanilla key. PMT reads the proposal from your localization: building_type_<old> points to the vanilla text with $building_type_<vanilla>$. For each building you see the proposal and a status; you can change the vanilla key. A row is blocked when the target is already defined in your mod, when vanilla defines it in a file your mod does not override, or when two buildings would get the same target.
patchhelp.adoptMod.warning: Careful: new building keys break running save games of your mod, buildings already built disappear. PMT asks before it goes ahead. Note the rename in your mod's changelog.
patchhelp.adoptMod.where: The rename runs over all files of your mod (.txt, .gui, .yml), whole words only. Derived names such as building_<key>, building_type_<key>, <key>_desc or has_variable = <key> are included; a longer key such as <key>_2 stays. With "Kommentar # was: <alter Schlüssel> einfügen", every renamed block gets the old name as its first line. The comment moves along when the block later goes into the generated region.
patchhelp.adoptMod.loc: PMT cleans up the localization at the same time, per language. For every line whose key changes:
patchhelp.adoptMod.locBox:
self-reference only    building_type_x: "$building_type_x$"  -> line removed, vanilla text applies
self-reference + text  "$cost$$building_type_x_desc$"       -> vanilla text inserted
already present        same text: line removed; other text: warning
vanilla has the key    -> localization/<language>/replace/pmt_renamed_l_<language>.yml
patchhelp.adoptMod.rows: After applying, the renamed buildings become rows of the table, but only vanilla specials that start an upgrade chain and have a place in history. PMT takes the holdings column from the current lists in your 00_holdings.txt. Then the preview shows the recipe run: it adopts the blocks like "Bestehende Blöcke übernehmen", and your values stay as hand edits. Localization keys of old levels without a building (e.g. building_<old>_1 when only _0 exists) are left unchanged; the window shows how many.
patchhelp.adoptMod.undo: Ctrl+Z undoes the file rename, but not the new table rows. Remove them by hand then, or the next recipe run puts vanilla copies next to the old keys.
patchhelp.adoptMod.after: Afterwards: vanilla scripts with add_special_building or has_special_building now point at converted buildings. The watcher reports them as new hits, and the slots rule copies more history files. Check both after the first recipe run.
patchhelp.table.files: In the “Files” field you separate several patterns with ;, for example history/provinces/*.txt;events/flogi_events.txt. This applies to columns and rules.
patchhelp.watch.heading: The watcher
patchhelp.watch.intro: The “Watcher” tab lists every file in vanilla and in your mod that uses a search pattern or a key of the table. This way you find places your recipe does not cover yet, also after a vanilla update. You set the search patterns under “Search patterns”; the watcher always also searches the keys of the table rows. Comments and the regions generated by the recipe do not count.
patchhelp.watch.statusBox:
not covered  A hit remains after applying, or vanilla has a hit
             and the mod gets no copy.
             Action: Create copy + rule, Ignore
outdated     The Update tool would offer the mod copy in
             “Merge after game update”.
             Action: Open in the Update tool
own file     File only in your mod, with hits.
             Action: Open (jumps to the line)
covered      No hit remains after applying.
ignored      Hidden by you, with a note.
             Action: Stop ignoring
patchhelp.watch.copy: “Create copy + rule” only changes the recipe: the file is added to a line rule of your choice, and “Create a copy from vanilla” is turned on there. The copy is created on the next apply. “New line rule (off)” creates a rule for the file that is still switched off. Check search and action before you turn it on: “Comment out” on a line with { would break the file.
patchhelp.watch.copyNarrow: If the chosen rule has a file pattern with * and does not create copies yet, PMT adds an identical rule right after it for this file only. This way only this one file is copied from vanilla, not every file the pattern matches.
patchhelp.watch.rescan: The watcher scans when you first open the tab and on “Scan again”. If rules, rows or search patterns change, the top says “Recipe changed, scan again”. Ignoring takes effect at once. “Hide done” hides covered and ignored files. Double-clicking a finding opens the file at that line.
patchhelp.update.watch: Then use “Scan again” in the watcher: new findings from vanilla show up as “not covered”.

generatorhelp.title: Guide: generator packages
generatorhelp.intro.heading: What are generator packages for?
generatorhelp.intro.what: A generator package turns a form into many mod files at once: own files, localization in all languages, sections in existing files, and images. Example IV2: a country's tag, coat of arms and ideas become 18 files.
generatorhelp.intro.how: The package describes form and outputs once. After that you only fill in the form in the window "Generator packages", per country or whatever the package's key is. PMT shows a preview and writes everything as one undo step.
generatorhelp.intro.editor: In the package editor you create packages and edit them with masks, without writing JSON. The running example of this guide is an invented package "City arms":
generatorhelp.intro.box:
Package stadtwappen (EU V)

generatorhelp.steps.heading: Workflow
generatorhelp.steps.list:
1. Create the package: "New" in the package editor, id stadtwappen.
2. Form: head fields and levels with their fields.
3. Outputs: what is written into which file.
4. Templates: the text of each output, in Scriban.
5. "Check": loads the package as a trial and checks all templates.
6. "Test in generator": opens the generator window on this package. For testing choose the target "output folder".
generatorhelp.steps.save: Ctrl+S saves. A half-finished package can be saved too; "Check" shows the errors. The window title shows * while something is unsaved. Shipped packages like IV2 (🔒) are read-only; "Edit as copy" creates an own copy with a new id.
generatorhelp.basics.heading: Basics and targets
generatorhelp.basics.fields: The id is the package's folder name and can only be changed through a copy. The name appears in the package list, in every language. The game decides where the package lives and when it is listed. The key field is the head field whose value names a work state; for City arms it is tag, one work state per tag.
generatorhelp.basics.targets: Targets: "mod" writes directly into the mod folder. "output" writes into a chosen folder and first copies every mod file it changes there. With "output" you test safely; several keys collect in the same output folder.
generatorhelp.form.heading: Form: head, levels and fields
generatorhelp.form.levels: The form asks head fields once per work state, for example tag. Below that is a chain of levels: each level has fields and at most one child level. A countable level has between Min and Max elements that the user creates; the initial count applies to new work states. A fixed level has one element per row of a constants table.
generatorhelp.form.number: Every element has a number: without a number base field it is its index from 1; with one it is the value of that field in the parent level plus the index. This gives IV2 unique numbers across all categories:
generatorhelp.form.box:
categories  fixed, table categories (adm base 0, dip base 10, ...)
  ideas     countable 0 to 9, number base field base
    levels  countable 1 to 4

Idea 2 in dip has the number 12.
generatorhelp.form.types: Field types: text, multi-line text, number, yes/no, choice (values one per line), image (from an asset library, with "Choose coat of arms") and modifiers (multi-line, with "+ Modifier"). Required and pattern (regular expression) block generating while not met. So does a modifier line without a value ("key = "). "Multilingual" gives text fields a translations dialog.
generatorhelp.form.ids: The id of a field or level is its name in the templates: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. A changed id applies when you leave the box; templates that use the old name report an error on the next check.
generatorhelp.constants.heading: Constants
generatorhelp.constants.text: Constants are tables with rows and columns that the package brings along. A fixed level has one element per row, and the columns can be read in templates like fields, e.g. c.base. The column label may have a text per language ("Cell languages"); the form shows it as a heading. Renaming a table adjusts the levels that use it.
generatorhelp.languages.heading: Multilingual texts and language rules
generatorhelp.languages.texts: Package name, labels and messages are either one text for all languages or one text per language. The box shows the interface language; "Languages" opens all eight. If only English with the old text remains, it stays a plain text.
generatorhelp.languages.rules:
The language rules apply to multilingual fields and are defaults that every work state can change:
• Extend English: localization for all languages of the game profile, without a translation using the English text.
• Copy English: empty languages get the English text.
• English for missing: if an entry has translations, its missing languages get the English text.
generatorhelp.assets.heading: Assets and origin
generatorhelp.assets.text: Assets are zip files or folders in the package's data folder, for example a coat of arms library. Image fields choose from them, copyBinary outputs copy from them. "Choose file" copies a file into the assets folder and sets the path; the status shows whether the file is there.
generatorhelp.assets.origin: Origin: "Game" means from the game files; such assets are never exported. "Mod/own" means from a mod or self-made; you may include those in an export. Without a statement "Game" applies. Do not pass on images from the game, not even by hand.
generatorhelp.outputs.heading: Output kinds
generatorhelp.outputs.intro: Every output has an id, a kind and a path. The path is a Scriban template relative to the mod and must stay inside the mod: a path with .., a drive or a leading / is an error. With "Per element" the output is made once per element of a level; in the template the element is called item.
generatorhelp.outputs.ownFile: Own file (ownFile): writes the whole file from the template.
generatorhelp.outputs.ownFileBox:
Path:      in_game/common/static_modifiers/sw_{{ tag }}.txt
Template:  modifiers.sbn

Result for tag = HAM:  in_game/common/static_modifiers/sw_HAM.txt
generatorhelp.outputs.localization: Localization (localization): one file per language; {{ lang }} in the path becomes the language. PMT adds l_<language>: when the template does not, and writes multilingual fields in the file's language, " as \" and line breaks as \n.
generatorhelp.outputs.insertSection: Insert section (insertSection): puts the text between markers into a block or at the end of the file. A second run replaces only the text between the markers. If the file is missing, the skeleton creates it.
generatorhelp.outputs.ensureLine: Ensure line (ensureLine): adds a line to a block when it is missing, e.g. has_or_had_tag = {{ tag }} in an OR list. No markers; an existing line stays untouched.
generatorhelp.outputs.syncBlocks: Sync blocks (syncBlocks): syncs top-level blocks whose key matches the key pattern (* = name characters). Missing ones are added, ones no longer generated are removed after a confirmation, and only the sub-keys from the template are replaced. With "Keep" (IV2: game_data) these sub-keys stay.
generatorhelp.outputs.copyBinary: Copy file (copyBinary): copies a file from an asset, e.g. the chosen coat of arms. The source is asset and entry, for example coa and {{ coa }}. An empty entry skips the output; if the library is missing, PMT skips it with a note.
generatorhelp.markers.heading: Block paths and markers
generatorhelp.markers.paths: A block path names keys separated by dots, e.g. sw_setup.sw_tags. In .gui files a header like types name, type name or template name also works; type name is searched in every types block of its level.
generatorhelp.markers.legacy: Legacy markers: if an older tool already wrote sections, legacy begin and legacy end name its markers. PMT finds and keeps them and only replaces the text in between. Legacy patterns are regular expressions for unmarked old entries; PMT removes them before inserting and states the count in the preview. Every pattern needs a fixed boundary after the key, e.g. _\d+, so that CA does not match CAS.
generatorhelp.markers.box:
IV2:
  Legacy begin:     # === IV2Generator:{{ tag }}:START ===
  Legacy end:       # === IV2Generator:{{ tag }}:END ===
  Legacy patterns:  ^\s*iv2_historic_idea_select_{{ tag }}_\d+
generatorhelp.templates.heading: Templates (Scriban)
generatorhelp.templates.names: Templates are Scriban texts in the templates folder. They know the head fields (tag), one list per level (ideas) with the fields of each element plus index, index0, first, last, number, suffix and parent, and also item, lang, constants, languages and language_rules. The list "Available names" on the right shows them all; a double click inserts the name.
generatorhelp.templates.whitespace: With -}} the line break after a tag is dropped; this keeps loops neat, one tag per line:
generatorhelp.templates.functions: functions.sbn holds own functions (func name ... end) that every template can use. Template texts are only written by "Save"; renaming and deleting save the package right away so that file and references match.
generatorhelp.templates.errors:
Common errors:
• An unknown name is an error with template and line, e.g. a typo in a field name.
• for or if without end.
• Forgotten }} in a path or block.
"Check" finds both: parse errors and, with a test run, unknown names.
generatorhelp.messages.heading: Warnings and errors
generatorhelp.messages.text: A condition is a Scriban expression. If a warning is true, the generator asks before generating; if an error is true, it refuses to generate. The message may have a text per language.
generatorhelp.messages.box:
Warning:  ideas.size < 3        Fewer than 3 ideas
Error:    ideas.size == 0       No idea created
generatorhelp.check.heading: Check and test
generatorhelp.check.check: "Check" loads the current state as a trial with the real loader and lets Scriban read all templates, paths, blocks and conditions. If everything parses, it renders each template once with sample values and so finds unknown names. A .yml output that is not of kind "Localization" is reported. The loader only reports its first error; check again after fixing it. A click on a template error jumps to the line.
generatorhelp.check.save: The first save writes package.json reformatted: same content, different layout. Comments in package.json are lost; PMT warns beforehand.
generatorhelp.check.test: "Test in generator" saves and opens the generator window on this package. Create a work state there, choose the target "output folder" and check the preview before you write into the mod.
generatorhelp.archive.heading: Export and import
generatorhelp.archive.export: "Export" writes the package as a .pmtgen file: package.json, functions.sbn and the templates always, work states and assets from mods on request. Assets from the game always stay out.
generatorhelp.archive.import: "Import" first shows what the file contains and creates the package in the folder of its game. If the id belongs to a shipped package, the import needs a new id. If an own package with the id exists, you choose replace (work states with the same name after a question) or a new id.
generatorhelp.archive.safety:
Safety:
• PMT reads only allowed entries: package.json, functions.sbn, templates, work states and files declared as mod assets.
• Entries with .., a drive or an absolute path are skipped and listed.
• PMT counts sizes while reading: package files at most 5 MB each and 50 MB in total, assets at most 1 GB each and 2 GB in total.
• Nothing is executed during import. The templates of someone else's package can only write into the mod or the output folder when generating; still check the preview.
generatorhelp.generator.heading: In the generator window
generatorhelp.generator.states: On the left you choose package and work state, on the right you fill in the form. "Preview" shows every file before and after; with U you take back marked changes. "Generate" writes everything as one undo step. "Edit package" opens the package in the package editor.
generatorhelp.generator.tools: If the package has a reader, "Read from mod" reads an existing set from the mod, "Take over tags from mod" creates work states for all keys, and "Check mod" compares mod and work states. "From database" takes names and descriptions from lookup sources, "+ Modifier" searches modifiers, and "Choose coat of arms" shows the images of a library.
generatorWindow.guide.tip: Opens the guide to generator packages (F1).
generators.error.templateName: Output {0}: template name "{1}" is invalid; only a file name ending in .sbn inside the templates folder is allowed.
packageEditor.basics.markerId.tip: ID in the markers PMT uses to find its sections in the mod again (# PMT-Generator <ID>/...). Empty = package ID. A copy keeps the original's ID, so it replaces the original's sections instead of writing them a second time. Enter an own ID only if the copy should write into the same mod separately from the original.
packageEditor.basics.markerId.invalid: Only lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40 characters. The change is applied only once the ID is valid.
packageEditor.basics.keySeparator.tip: Joins the values of several key fields, default _ (adm + 18 = adm_18).
packageEditor.basics.keyFields.needOne: At least one key field must be chosen.
packageEditor.basics.keyFields.tip: Head fields whose values name a work state, in head order. Example: tag (one work state per country) or category and number (adm_18). All but the last need a pattern or a choice.
generatorhelp.basics.markerId: The marker ID appears in the lines PMT uses to find its sections in the mod again (# PMT-Generator iv2/...). Empty means the package ID. "Edit as copy" and an import under a new ID enter the original's ID: that way the copy replaces the original's sections instead of writing them a second time. If an older copy has the field empty, enter the original's ID there, e.g. iv2.
generators.pattern.needsGroup: The pattern needs a group in round brackets for the tag.
generators.pattern.pathUnsafe: Path "{0}" must stay relative (no "..", no drive, no leading /).
generators.check.ymlNotLocalization: Output "{0}" writes a .yml file but is not of kind "localization". Only that kind writes one file per language with the header l_<language>:.
generators.check.expectedImage: an image field of the head
generators.check.expectedText: a text field of the same level
generators.probe.fileMissing: File "{0}" is missing in the mod.
generators.probe.noElementsFile: The elements file "{0}" is missing in the mod; there is nothing to read for this key.
generators.probe.noLocalizationOutput: The package has no output of the kind localization; texts are not read.
generators.preview.noBlocks: The .txt files contain no matching blocks (check depth and "Named blocks only").
generators.preview.itemsEmpty: The items path "{0}" matches nothing in the file.
packageEditor.read.enable: Package can read sets from a mod
packageEditor.read.enable.tip: Switches on "Read from mod", "Take over tags from mod" and "Check mod" in the generator window. The patterns below describe where PMT finds the values of a set in the mod.
packageEditor.read.disableConfirm: Remove the "Read back" section with all its patterns?
packageEditor.read.offNote: Without this section the generator can only create sets, not read them back from a mod.
packageEditor.read.keys.tip: Regular expression on the mod's paths (with /). Every matching file names one set with the group (?<key>...). Example: ^main_menu/common/static_modifiers/02_IV2_(?<key>[A-Z0-9]{2,5})\.txt$
packageEditor.read.valueJoin.tip: Characters between the values; empty or \n = line break.
packageEditor.read.valueField.tip: Text field that receives the values: a head field or level.field.
packageEditor.read.valueBody.tip: Instead of collecting hits, read the whole content of a sub-block, given as a path of keys. Example: allow (the conditions of an action).
packageEditor.read.flagPattern.tip: Regular expression with Scriban instead of the fixed text, e.g. with a number boundary: iv2_ga_select_ideagroup_{{ category }}_{{ group }}(?![0-9]).
packageEditor.read.valuePattern.tip: Regular expression with (?<value>...); every hit in the block gives one value. Example: religion = religion:(?<value>\w+)
packageEditor.read.valueBlock.tip: Pattern on the top-level block key. Example: iv2_ga_select_ideagroup_{{ category }}_{{ group }}
packageEditor.read.valueFile.tip: Mod file with the block, with Scriban for the key.
packageEditor.read.valuesNote: Collects hits from a block into a text field, e.g. all religions from religion = religion:x. Duplicates are dropped.
packageEditor.read.locOutput.tip: The localization output whose files are read.
packageEditor.read.keysBlock.tip: Regular expression on the top-level block keys. The group (?<key>...) or one group per key field with its name names the set. Example: ideagroup_modifier_(?<category>adm|dip|army|navy)_(?<group>\d+)_1
packageEditor.read.keysFile.tip: Regular expression on the mod's paths (with /): the block keys are read in these files. Example: ^main_menu/common/static_modifiers/01_IV2_ideagroup_modifiers_(adm|dip|army|navy)\.txt$
packageEditor.read.keysFrom.tip: File path: one file per set, the path names the set. Blocks in files: the sets live in shared files, the block keys name them.
packageEditor.read.elementsFile.tip: File of the mod with one block per element, with {{ tag }} for the key. Example: main_menu/common/static_modifiers/02_IV2_{{ tag }}.txt
packageEditor.read.elementsBlock.tip: Pattern on the keys of the top-level blocks of this file. (?<number>...) is the element's number, (?<suffix>...) picks the element of the deeper level. Example: national_idea_modifier_{{ tag }}_(?<number>\d+)(?<suffix>_\d)?
packageEditor.read.elementsLevel.tip: Level whose elements are created from the blocks.
packageEditor.read.body.tip: The field gets the block's lines (comments and sub-blocks included, common indentation removed).
packageEditor.read.except.tip: Keys whose lines are not taken, separated by commas. Example: game_data
packageEditor.read.localizationNote: PMT reads the file of the localization output in every language of the game profile. English fills the field, other languages become translations.
packageEditor.read.locKey.tip: Pattern on localization keys with (?<number>...). Example: iv2_historic_idea_{{ tag }}_(?<number>\d+)
packageEditor.read.locField.tip: Multilingual text field that receives the text: a head field or level.field.
packageEditor.read.flagFile.tip: File of the mod with the blocks that carry the flag. Example: in_game/common/generic_actions/iv2_GA_ideas_{{ tag }}.txt
packageEditor.read.flagBlock.tip: Pattern on the block keys of this file, with (?<number>...) and, if needed, (?<suffix>...).
packageEditor.read.contains.tip: If this text is in the block, the field becomes "Yes", otherwise "No". Example: for_nat_idea_expensive_
packageEditor.read.assetField.tip: Image field of the head. PMT looks in its asset library for the entry with the same bytes as the mod's file.
packageEditor.read.assetFile.tip: Image file of the mod. Example: main_menu/gfx/interface/coa/{{ tag }}.dds
packageEditor.read.suggest.tip: Builds the pattern from an example in the mod: click a file, block or localization key, PMT replaces the key and the number.
packageEditor.read.suggest.readOnly: Shipped packages stay unchanged. The suggested pattern to copy:
packageEditor.read.probe.tip: Reads one set from a mod with the current patterns and shows the matches per pattern and the result. Writes nothing.
packageEditor.read.chooseMod.message: Which mod should the examples come from? The active mod is at the top.
packageEditor.read.noMods: No mod with an existing folder is known.
packageEditor.read.chooseKey.message: Which set should the probe run read?
packageEditor.read.probeNoKeys: The key files pattern finds no set in this mod.
packageEditor.suggest.title: Suggest pattern
packageEditor.suggest.keyValue.tip: The key field's value that occurs in the example, e.g. BYZ. It becomes {{ tag }} or (?<key>...).
packageEditor.suggest.file.tip: File of the mod whose top-level blocks are listed below.
packageEditor.suggest.keyMissing: The key does not occur in the example as a word of its own.
packageEditor.probe.title: Probe run: {0}
packageEditor.lookups.intro: Sources for "From database": a field names one or more sources, and the generator shows their entries in a table with a search field. Sources read blocks from the game folder or entries from a JSON file of the package.
packageEditor.lookups.new.tip: Creates a new source "From the game"; the kind can be changed afterwards.
packageEditor.lookups.duplicate.tip: Creates a copy of the selected source with a new id.
packageEditor.lookups.remove.tip: Removes the selected source and takes it out of all fields.
packageEditor.lookups.removeConfirm: The source "{0}" is used by {1} fields. Remove it and take it out of these fields?
packageEditor.lookups.id.tip: Id of the source; fields name it under "From database". Renaming updates the fields. Example: advances
packageEditor.lookups.label: Label
packageEditor.lookups.label.tip: Shown as "Type" in the "From database" table. Example: Advance
packageEditor.lookups.kind.tip: "From the game" reads blocks from .txt files of the game folder and their official texts. "JSON file" reads entries from a file the package names as an asset.
packageEditor.lookups.kindChanged: The entries of the previous kind were removed.
packageEditor.lookups.folder.tip: Folder relative to the game content; every .txt file in it is read. Example: in_game/common/advances
packageEditor.lookups.depth.tip: 1 = only top-level blocks become entries; 2 = also their direct sub-blocks (e.g. laws and their policies).
packageEditor.lookups.namedOnly.tip: Only blocks whose key has a text in the localization. This leaves out blocks like potential.
packageEditor.lookups.tagFromFile.tip: Regular expression on the file name; group 1 is the tag. Example: ^country_([A-Za-z]{2,5})\.txt$
packageEditor.lookups.tagInBlock.tip: Keys whose value in the block is a tag, separated by commas; used when the file name gives no tag. Example: has_or_had_tag, tag
packageEditor.lookups.asset.tip: JSON file from the package's asset list (Assets section).
packageEditor.lookups.items.tip: Way to the entries in the JSON file; name[] steps into every element of a list. Example: nations[].ideas[]
packageEditor.lookups.field.tip: Property of the entry in the JSON file; ../x reads x from the parent element. Empty = stays empty.
packageEditor.lookups.entry.name: Name
packageEditor.lookups.preview.tip: Reads the source with the current state like "From database" and shows the count and the first 50 entries.
packageEditor.lookup.enable.tip: Shows "From database" next to the field: an entry from the chosen sources fills name and description.
packageEditor.lookup.sources.tip: Sources from "Lookups" whose entries the table shows; at least one.
packageEditor.lookup.noSources: The package has no source yet. Create them under "Lookups".
packageEditor.lookup.fill.tip: Text field of the same level that gets the entry's name or description. Set at least one.
generatorhelp.read.heading: Read back (Read from mod)
generatorhelp.read.intro: With the "Read back" section the generator reads a set that a mod already contains back into the form. "Read from mod", "Take over tags from mod" and "Check mod" use it. The patterns are regular expressions; {{ tag }} stands for the key.
generatorhelp.read.steps:
Step by step:
• Key files: pattern on the mod's paths; the group (?<key>...) names the set.
• Elements: a file with one block per element and a block pattern with (?<number>...). The number finds the element as when generating (base plus index); (?<suffix>...) picks the element of the deeper level.
• For each field of the level, "Take block content" puts the block's lines into the field; "Exceptions" leaves out keys such as game_data.
• Localization, yes/no flags and images fill further fields.
generatorhelp.read.box:
Key files:     ^in_game/common/static_modifiers/sw_(?<key>[A-Z]{3})\.txt$
File:          in_game/common/static_modifiers/sw_{{ tag }}.txt
Block pattern: sw_modifier_{{ tag }}_(?<number>\d+)
Level:         ideas; modifiers: take block content, exceptions game_data
Localization:  sw_{{ tag }}_(?<number>\d+)  ->  ideas.name
generatorhelp.read.suggest: "Suggest" builds a pattern from an example: choose a mod, then click a file, a block or a localization key. PMT replaces the key (e.g. HAM) with {{ tag }} or (?<key>...), the first number after it with (?<number>\d+) and a _1 at the end with (?<suffix>_\d+)?. For blocks with levels pick an example with an ending, otherwise the suffix group is missing.
generatorhelp.read.probe: "Probe run" reads one set from a chosen mod with the current patterns, without saving or writing. The "Matches" tab shows what each pattern finds; a pattern without matches is shown as a warning. "Result" shows the read state, "Notes" the reader's messages, e.g. numbers outside every group. All paths stay inside the mod: the reader skips paths with .., a drive or a leading /.
generatorhelp.shared.box:
Output:         Sync by match, block "types iv2_ideagroups_adm_all"
Match pattern:  type iv2_ig_{{ category }}_{{ group }}(?![0-9])
Localization:   key pattern ^iv2_ga_ideagroup_{{ category }}_{{ group }}(_|$)
Read back:      keys from blocks, ideagroup_modifier_(?<category>adm|dip)_(?<group>\d+)_1
generatorhelp.shared.keys: Keys from several fields: under "Basics" several key fields can be chosen, e.g. category (choice) and number; the key is then adm_18. When reading back, the keys come from blocks in files, head fields like the title from the localization, and "Collect values" reads e.g. all religions of a group.
generatorhelp.shared.localization: Localization with "Key pattern (shared file)": PMT replaces only the lines whose key matches and keeps all other lines of the file. Without a pattern a localization writes the whole file as before, which deletes all other sets in a shared file.
generatorhelp.shared.match: "Sync by match" (syncMatching): the entries of a block (or of the file) are units: statements, GUI headers with their body, list values, unnamed blocks and comment lines of their own. Every unit whose text the match pattern hits belongs to the set; PMT replaces it in place with the template's text, without markers. Without a hit the text goes to the end of the block. Boundaries belong in the pattern so that adm_1 does not hit adm_18. The template writes the indentation the file has at that spot.
generatorhelp.shared.check: "Check" (check) writes nothing: each line of the template is "pattern => argument". After all other outputs PMT searches every pattern in the planned text of the file; when it finds nothing, the preview shows the message as a warning, with {{ arg }} for the argument. This can report, for example, that a partner group does not exclude this group yet and has to be generated again. When texts live in a second shared localization file, each reading entry names its own "Output".
packageEditor.output.message.tip: Warning in the preview when a pattern of the check finds nothing. Scriban; {{ arg }} is the argument after => in the template line.
packageEditor.read.locEntryOutput.tip: Localization output whose files this entry reads. Default: the output chosen above.
generatorhelp.shared.intro: Some sets have no files of their own but are spread across files they share with all others, like the idea groups of Idea Variation 2: one group sits in about 30 files, as blocks, GUI types, list entries, unnamed if blocks and localization lines. Three building blocks handle this.
generatorhelp.shared.heading: Shared files
generatorhelp.lookups.heading: Lookups (From database)
generatorhelp.lookups.intro: Lookup sources provide entries for "From database": key, name, description, tag and nation. A text field names its sources under "Look up in database" together with the fields that get name and description.
generatorhelp.lookups.game: "From the game" reads every .txt file in the folder of the game content. Depth 1 takes the top-level blocks, depth 2 also their sub-blocks. "Named blocks only" leaves out blocks without a localization text. Name and description come from the game's localization (<key> and <key>_desc), also in the other languages of the work state.
generatorhelp.lookups.gameBox:
Id:                  advances
Kind:                From the game
Folder:              in_game/common/advances
Depth:               1
Tag from file name:  ^country_([A-Za-z]{2,5})\.txt$
Tag in block:        has_or_had_tag, tag
generatorhelp.lookups.json: "JSON file" reads a file that the package names as an asset. The items path leads to the entries; name[] steps into every element of a list. The mapping names the property for each entry field; ../x reads x from the parent element:
generatorhelp.lookups.preview: "Preview" reads the source like the generator and shows the count and the first 50 entries. If nothing comes, the reason is shown: game folder missing, asset file missing, folder without .txt files or a path that matches nothing. Folders stay inside the game folder; a folder with .. is refused.
generatorhelp.lookups.field: In the mask of a text field, "Look up in database" switches on the "From database" button in the generator. Choose the sources and the fields of the same level that get name and description; at least one. When you rename a source or a field, the references follow.
generators.ai.fileNotAllowed: File "{0}" is not allowed (only package.json, functions.sbn and templates/*.sbn without sub-folders).
generators.ai.blockWithoutEnd: The block for "{0}" does not end with <<<END>>>.
generators.ai.noFiles: The answer contains no file blocks (<<<FILE path>>> ... <<<END>>>).
aiPackage.title: Create package with AI
aiPackage.open.tip: Assembles a task for an AI of your choice (guide, example files from your mod, description) and takes its answer back as a package.
aiPackage.taskIntro: 1. Choose a mod and tick the files of one finished set (e.g. everything for one tag), or paste only the relevant parts under "Code blocks". 2. Describe what the form should ask for. 3. Copy the task and paste it into an AI, or save it as a folder for an AI with file access. 4. Paste the answer under "Result".
aiPackage.mod.tip: Mod with the example; the active mod is preselected.
aiPackage.chooseMod.message: Choose the mod with the example. The active mod is at the top.
aiPackage.files.tip: Tick all files of one finished set, including localization and entries in shared files. Images are only named, not sent.
aiPackage.chosen.tip: Untick a file to take it out of the task again.
aiPackage.clearChosen.tip: Takes all ticked files out of the task.
aiPackage.snippets.tip: Paste only the relevant parts instead of whole files. This keeps the task small, even for free AIs.

generatorhelp.ai.heading: Create with AI
generatorhelp.ai.intro: Building a package by hand is a lot of work. "Create with AI" (in the package editor and the generator window) hands this work to an AI of your choice: PMT assembles the task, the AI writes package.json and the templates, PMT takes the answer back and checks it.
generatorhelp.ai.steps:
In five steps:
1. Choose a mod and tick the files of one finished set, e.g. everything for one tag, including localization and entries in shared files.
2. Describe what the form should ask for.
3. "Copy as text" and paste it into a chat AI, or "Save as folder" for an AI with file access.
4. Paste the answer under "Result" and press "Apply" (or import the AI's folder).
5. If "Check" reports errors, "Copy errors for the AI" and give them back to the AI until everything fits. Then "Test in generator".
generatorhelp.ai.snippets: Large files quickly overwhelm free chat AIs. Then paste only the relevant parts in the tab "Code blocks", each with the path of its file in the mod ("Choose from mod") and its scope: "Whole file", or "Excerpt" when the rest of the file should stay. Files and code blocks can be mixed. The blocks stay while the window is open; "Save as file" keeps the whole task.
generatorhelp.ai.snippetTools: Each block can get a "Note": it tells the AI what matters about exactly this block, e.g. "repeats per idea". "Take from mod file" and "Take from game file" open a file; the selected lines become a new block with its path. Blocks from the game are marked as "Game file" and serve the AI as a model. A click on the header line collapses a block; "Collapse all" keeps long lists tidy.
generatorhelp.ai.tips:
Tips:
• Choose a complete example: a missing file is missing in the package.
• Start small, e.g. only modifiers and localization, then extend.
• With "Include the open package" the AI changes an existing package; id and marker id stay.
• The guide for the AI is in the program folder under ai-guide/generator-packages (also usable as a Claude skill).
generatorhelp.ai.cli:
For AIs with file access, pmt-generator.exe is in the program folder:
• check <package folder>: loads and checks the package like "Check".
• probe <package folder> <mod folder> [<key>]: probe run of reading back.
• roundtrip <package folder> <mod folder> <key>: reads a set from the mod, generates it again and compares every file. If everything matches, the package is right.
The command never writes into the mod or the package.
