generatorhelp.form.autoNumber: Automatic number (autoNumber): the last key field of type number in the head can be set to "Automatic number", for example the number of an idea group. "New state" fills in the highest number that the work states and reading know for the other key parts, plus 1; you can overwrite it. Before the preview PMT checks the hashes of the localization keys: if a new state collides with a key of the game or the mod, it moves to the next number without a collision. A key the mod already has is never renumbered and only gets a warning.
generatorhelp.outputs.jsonEntry: JSON entry (jsonEntry): sets one entry in a JSON file outside the mod, for example in the tag list of a helper script. The file is listed under "External files" and you choose its path in the generator window; the output needs no path. "JSON path" is the dot path to the object in the file (empty = the root object), "Entry key" is the key in it, and the template renders the value as JSON. An existing key is replaced in place, a new key is appended at the end; the rest of the file stays byte-identical.
generatorhelp.externals.heading: External files and hint
generatorhelp.externals.text: The "External files" section lists files outside the mod that outputs of kind jsonEntry write into. Each has an id, a label and a hint (tooltip) per language. The path is not stored in the package: the generator window shows a row per file with "Choose file" and remembers the path per package. If no file is chosen or it is missing, PMT skips the output with a warning. When generating, PMT first copies the old file to a backups folder next to it and does not write if the file changed since the preview. "Check mod" ignores these files.
generatorhelp.externals.afterGenerate: Hint after generating (afterGenerate): the text appears in the generator window below the message when generating succeeded, for example as a reminder of a helper script that has to run next. It does not appear on errors or when cancelled.
generatorhelp.shared.insertAfter: "Insert after" (insertAfter, also for localization with a key pattern): without it a new set goes to the end of the block. With this pattern (a regular expression with Scriban, tested against the text of each unit, or against the key for localization) it goes right after the last unit that matches, for example after the previous group, so the order in the file is right. This only applies while no unit of the set exists yet; existing ones keep their place. If the pattern matches nothing, the default position applies.
generatorhelp.shared.ifLimit: "Condition (if/limit)" (ifLimit, only for sync by match): some files group entries in if blocks with a limit condition. The condition template (Scriban, one line per condition) decides where the text belongs: rendered empty it goes on the top level, otherwise into the if block with exactly this condition, which PMT creates if it does not exist yet. If the condition changes, the set moves, and an if block left empty by that disappears. The template then indents one level deeper.
packageEditor.externals.note: Files outside the mod that outputs of kind "JSON entry" (jsonEntry) write an entry into. You choose the path in the generator window; it is not stored in the package.
packageEditor.externals.id.tip: Name of the file in the package; the output names it under "External file". Example: tags.
packageEditor.externals.label: Label
packageEditor.externals.label.tip: How the file is called in the generator window, next to the button to choose it. Example: Tag list.
packageEditor.externals.hint.tip: Appears as a tooltip at the file choice in the generator window. Example: The file tags.json in the folder of the helper script.
packageEditor.externals.remove.tip: Removes the entry; outputs that name it report this when checking.
packageEditor.afterGenerate.note: This text appears in the generator window below the message when generating succeeded, for example as a reminder of a step that follows outside PMT.
packageEditor.afterGenerate.label: Hint
packageEditor.afterGenerate.tip: Text per language, no Scriban. Empty = no hint. Example: Then run the helper script build_chooser.py.
packageEditor.candidates.note: For the "Modifiers without idea…" button in the generator window: how to tell that a modifier is already used, how the list is split into groups, and how a modifier becomes a work state. "Check" tests the rules of this section.
packageEditor.candidates.add.tip: Adds the section empty; "Check" reports what is still missing.
packageEditor.candidates.category.tip: Where the modifiers come from: the category in the game's modifier definitions and the scope in the script database. Empty and "all" do not count. Example: country.
packageEditor.candidates.used.heading: Where a modifier is used
packageEditor.candidates.used.note: A modifier counts as used when it stands directly in a matching block of a matching file of the mod. At least one entry is required.
packageEditor.candidates.used.file.tip: Regular expression on the relative path of the file in the mod. Example: ^common/static_modifiers/.*[.]txt$
packageEditor.candidates.used.block.tip: Regular expression on the whole key of the top-level block. Example: ^iv2_.*$
packageEditor.candidates.used.except.tip: Sub-blocks that do not count, separated by commas. Example: game_data
packageEditor.candidates.used.add.tip: New entry: the file and block in which a modifier counts as used.
packageEditor.candidates.groups.heading: Groups
packageEditor.candidates.groups.note: The window splits the modifiers into groups by their name. The order matters: the first group whose pattern matches wins; whatever fits none is shown under "General". Write patterns with name-part boundaries, e.g. (^|_)(word|...)(_|$), not as a bare substring.
packageEditor.candidates.group.id.tip: Unique name of the group; the window remembers under it whether the group is hidden. Example: estates.
packageEditor.candidates.group.label: Label
packageEditor.candidates.group.label.tip: How the group is called in the window's list, per language. Empty = the id. Example: Estates.
packageEditor.candidates.group.pattern.t: Regular expression on the name of the modifier. Example: (^|_)(nobles|clergy|burghers)(_|$)
packageEditor.candidates.group.hidden.ti: The window first shows the group greyed out; the user can show it.
packageEditor.candidates.group.add.tip: New group at the end of the list; move it to the right place with Up and Down.
packageEditor.candidates.group.remove.ti: Removes this group; its modifiers fall into the next matching group or into "General".
packageEditor.candidates.create.heading: Creating work states
packageEditor.candidates.ask.tip: Head fields of type choice that the user picks once for all new work states, separated by commas. Every key field except the one with the automatic number must be listed. Example: category, subTab
packageEditor.candidates.name: Name field
packageEditor.candidates.name.tip: Head field of type text that receives the official name of the modifier. Example: name
packageEditor.candidates.modifiers.tip: Field of type modifiers of a level, as level.field; the modifier goes on all levels. Example: levels.modifiers
packageEditor.candidates.remove.tip: Removes the whole candidates section; the package then has no "Modifiers without idea…" button.
packageEditor.field.autoNumber.tip: A new work state gets the next free number in this field; localization keys with the same hash move on. Only on the last key field of type number in the head.
packageEditor.field.autoNumberNotLast: autoNumber is only allowed on the last key field; this field is not one (Basics, key fields).
packageEditor.output.insertAfter.tip: Regular expression (with Scriban): new entries go right after the last entry whose text (for localization: whose key) it matches; existing ones keep their place. Without a match the default position applies. For localization only with a key pattern. Example: ^iv2_ga_ideagroup_{{ category }}_1.
packageEditor.output.ifLimit.tip: Scriban template with the text of a condition. Rendered empty: the entries stay on the top level. Otherwise they go into an if = { limit = { ... } } with this condition, and the template then indents one level deeper. One line per condition. Example: has_variable = iv2_flag_{{ category }}.
packageEditor.output.external.tip: Id of a file from "External files" that the entry is written into. You choose the path in the generator window.
packageEditor.output.jsonPath.tip: Dot path of the objects in the file that hold the entry (Scriban). Empty = the root object. Example: entries.
packageEditor.output.entryKey.tip: Key of the entry in the object (Scriban). An existing key is replaced in place, a new key is appended at the end. Example: {{ tag }}.
packageEditor.output.jsonTemplate.tip: Scriban template from the templates folder that renders the value of the entry as JSON.
packageEditor.output.jsonEntryNote: This kind writes into an external file outside the mod and needs no path.

generatorWindow.candidates.onlyNew.tip: Only modifiers that the latest import of the script database added.
generatorWindow.candidates.customHide.ti: Regular expression on the key: matches are hidden, in addition to the hidden groups. Applies to this package.
generatorWindow.candidates.notAsIdea.tip: Marks the chosen modifiers as “not as idea”; they are then hidden in every view. “Show hidden” shows them greyed, and “Show again” undoes the mark.
generatorWindow.candidates.create.tip: Creates a new work state for each chosen modifier. The values stay empty.
generatorWindow.candidates.ask.title: Create work states
generatorWindow.candidates.ask.message: These entries apply to all {0} new work states. PMT assigns the numbers in sequence.
generatorWindow.candidates.names.title: Reading the modifier names
generatorWindow.candidates.names.hint: Reads the official name of the modifiers in each language of the work state from the localisation of game and mod.
generatorhelp.candidates.heading: Modifiers without idea
generatorhelp.candidates.text:
The “Modifiers without idea…” button appears for packages with a candidates section (e.g. IV2 dynamic ideas). It lists the game's modifiers that no idea of the mod uses yet.
• Used: A modifier counts as used if it stands in one of the blocks of the mod that the package names. Commented-out lines do not count. For IV2 these are the blocks national_idea_modifier_<category>_<number> in the four files 01_IV2_dynamic_national_ideas_<category>.txt; old country ideas and idea groups do not count.
• new: The mark ✱ shows modifiers that the latest import of the script database added. “New only” shows just these.
• Groups: The package sorts the modifiers into groups (left). Whatever fits none is under “General”; “All” shows everything. The search always covers all groups and also finds modifiers in hidden groups.
• Hiding: The tick “hide” hides a group, for IV2 e.g. the goods groups. It stays on the left, greyed and with its counts, so that a new modifier in it does not go unnoticed. On top of that there is your own regex above the list, which hides modifiers by key. If you select a hidden group on the left, the list shows its modifiers anyway. “Show hidden” brings everything back, also the modifiers marked “not as idea” and those hit by the regex.
• Not as idea: Marks chosen modifiers that should not become an idea. They are then hidden in every view, also in their own group; “Show hidden” shows them greyed, and “Show again” undoes the mark.
• Work state: If a modifier already stands in a work state of the package, the “Work state” column names its key.
• Create…: Creates a work state for each chosen modifier. If one already stands in a work state, PMT asks first. PMT asks the requested entries once (for IV2 category and sub-tab) and assigns the numbers in sequence. The name is the official name of the modifier in each language. The modifier stands on all levels; a yes/no modifier on one level with yes.
The values stay empty on purpose: you enter them yourself. “Generate” refuses empty values until all are filled in.
